feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, 51.31) gave the best s-bend progress (0.155) but one line-loss event per run on s-bend and slalom, with steering_oscillation 0.127 and 0.138. Slalom oscillation stayed at about 0.14 at y=0.05, 0.06 and 0.07 m (iterations 3 to 5), so the lead is not its cause. The oval has been stuck at progress 0.115 and max_error 0.061 m since iteration 1 under every geometry change tried, so geometry alone may not fix it. What I had to compensate for: I kept kp 2.0 and kd 0.10 because the narrower 0.09 m track already raises turn gain, and I kept ki 0 to avoid windup on bends. Next race: if line_loss_events return on s-bend or slalom at wheel_radius 0.04 m, ground speed is too high for the lead. Then return wheel_radius to 0.03 m and try a slightly larger sensor lead of y=0.065 m. If steering_oscillation stays above 0.10 on slalom with zero line loss, the speed is not the cause and I will change the controller, not the geometry. If slalom max_error is above 0.06 m, widen the spread.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events rise on s-bend or slalom at wheel_radius 0.04 m (iteration 3 had 1 per run at 0.03 m), return wheel_radius to 0.03 m and set sensor y to 0.065 m to keep the lead while cutting speed.

If slalom max_error stays above 0.06 m (iteration 3 gave 0.065 m, iteration 4 gave 0.068 m), widen sensor x to +/-0.065 m with sensor_size 0.016 m, so the line stays under the sensors on slalom bends.

If the score is at or below 51.3 with s-bend progress near 0.15, keep the lead at y=0.07 m and try sensor_size 0.012 m, to test whether a smaller footprint reduces the signal jitter that the 16 mm footprint may add.
